title: Number game: Ex-DGP-turned-councillor's resignation move puts BJP on a sticky wicket in T'puram Corporation - The South First
content: Published Oct 04, 2026 | 12:00 PM ⚊ Updated Oct 04, 2026 | 12:01 PM R Sreelekha flanked by Mayor VV Rajesh and Deputy Mayor Asha Nath GS Synopsis: The BJP’s historic capture of Thiruvananthapuram Corporation is suddenly on shaky ground as party councillor and former DGP R Sreelekha moves to quit, putting its wafer-thin majority at risk. With the party’s one-seat majority hanging by a thread, Sreelekha makes her move, and the BJP counts its pieces. In December 2025, Prime Minister Narendra Modi had called the BJP’s capture of the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation a “watershed moment” in Keralam politics. Ten months later, that watershed victory is facing a serious test — and the trouble is from within. R. Sreelekha, the former DGP who was brought into the BJP with considerable political expectations and projected as one of its most recognisable faces in the capital, has announced her resignation as a councillor. If she stands firm on quitting, her exit comes at a particularly awkward moment for the BJP, which governs the 101-member Corporation with a one-seat cushion. Her resignation threat has once again exposed just how fragile the arithmetic behind the BJP’s historic victory remains. The party has 50 councillors and depends on independent Pattoor Radhakrishnan to reach the 51-member mark needed to retain control. With Sreelekha’s resignation, the BJP’s tally could fall to 49, leaving the NDA camp with 50 members. That makes the Sasthamangalam ward more than just another vacancy. A by-election there could determine whether the BJP can hold on to the Corporation it fought for decades to capture. For the BJP, the political irony is hard to miss. Sreelekha was inducted into the party in October 2024, elevated as a state vice-president. There was even an expectation that she could emerge as the party’s mayoral face after winning Sasthamangalam. Instead, VV Rajesh took the mayor’s post, while Asha Nath GS became the Deputy Mayor, leaving Sreelekha as just another councillor in the council she had been expected to lead. Her resignation announcement, therefore, comes less than a year after the BJP celebrated its biggest municipal breakthrough in Keralam. What began as the rise of a high-profile recruit now threatens to become an internal test of the party’s hold over the capital corporation. The question now is not merely why Sreelekha walked out. It is whether the BJP can absorb her exit, if it indeed happens, without allowing the narrow arithmetic that brought it to power in Thiruvananthapuram to unravel. Also Read: BJP’s civic majority in Thiruvananthapuram jolted as Sreelekha submits resignation to Mayor Sreelekha may have announced her resignation, but technically she continues to hold office, with the resignation yet to be submitted in the manner prescribed under the Kerala Municipality Act 1994. Sreelekha’s WhatsApp message announcing her resignation Sreelekha announced in a WhatsApp group formed for the Sasthamangalam ward that she had decided to resign for “personal reasons” and had handed over her resignation letter to Mayor Rajesh on 30 September. She said a copy would be submitted to the District Collector on 5 October. However, the Mayor and Corporation officials maintained that no formal resignation had reached the Corporation Secretary, the competent authority under the law to receive a councillor’s resignation. Rajesh sought to play down the development, saying Sreelekha had handed him a letter detailing certain personal difficulties. He stopped short of confirming that it was a resignation letter, pointing out that a councillor has to submit the resignation to the Corporation Secretary. Corporation Secretary J Muhammed Shafi also said no such communication had been received. Under Section 40 of the Kerala Municipality Act, 1994, a councillor has to tender the resignation to the Secretary in the prescribed form. The resignation takes effect from the date the Secretary receives it, following which the fact has to be reported to the council and the State Election Commission. A Corporation official said Sreelekha had “announced” her resignation, but had not initiated the formal process. “The councillor may submit the resignation directly to the Secretary or send it by registered post, with the prescribed attestation where required. The Secretary has to acknowledge its receipt. None of that has happened in this case,” the official said. The BJP leadership, meanwhile, is understood to be in touch with Sreelekha in an effort to address her grievances. Party sources said the fact that the letter was handed over to the Mayor and not the Corporation Secretary had left room for discussions and efforts to persuade her to reconsider. Rajesh said the party was examining the concerns raised by Sreelekha and trying to find a way forward. “On the basis of the letter I got and the information shared with me, I’m trying to take things forward smoothly and address them in the way possible,” he said. For now, therefore, Sreelekha has announced her resignation, but has not formally resigned from the Corporation. Also Read: BJP councilor R Sreelekha opts out of PM-hosted Delhi visit The BJP’s historic capture of the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation could soon enter a more uncertain phase, with Sreelekha’s resignation threatening to strip the ruling NDA of its wafer-thin majority. Sreelekha’s decision to quit as councillor from Sasthamangalam has changed the arithmetic of the 101-member council. If the resignation is formally moved, the BJP’s strength will come down to 49. With the support of independent councillor Pattoor Radhakrishnan, who represents Kannammoola, the NDA will have 50 members — one short of the majority mark. That leaves the BJP with a difficult stretch ahead. The party’s biggest gain in the 2025 local-body elections was winning 50 of the corporation’s 101 wards, emerging as the single largest party. But 50 was not enough to form the council on its own. Radhakrishnan’s decision to support the BJP-led NDA provided the crucial 51st vote and paved the way for the BJP to take control of the corporation for the first time. Sreelekha’s exit threatens to undo that arithmetic. For the moment, the BJP’s immediate task is to prevent the resignation from becoming final. If she remains firm, the party will have to keep the council functioning without a majority and, at the same time, prepare for the Sasthamangalam by-election. That election could become the BJP’s most important political battle in the corporation. A BJP victory would restore its strength to 50 and, with the independent’s support, take the NDA back to the 51 needed for a majority. A defeat, on the other hand, could prolong the uncertainty and give the opposition an opening to test the stability of the Rajesh-led administration. The BJP is already dealing with another vacancy-like situation. Its councillor from Vazhottukonam, R Sugathan, is in jail in connection with a case under the Kerala Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act (KAAPA). His absence has complicated the ruling front’s position in council proceedings. He has been granted six months’ leave to avoid disqualification arising from prolonged absence from council meetings. The opposition had already tested the waters earlier this year. The UDF had planned to move a no-confidence motion against the BJP-led council in June. But with only 20 councillors, it needed the LDF’s support to take the move forward. The LDF, which has 29 members, did not agree to back the initiative, forcing the UDF to drop the plan. Sreelekha’s resignation now brings the question back into focus. The LDF and UDF together have 49 councillors — exactly the strength the BJP would have after Sreelekha’s resignation. Whether that arithmetic can translate into a change of administration, however, will depend entirely on whether the two fronts are willing to work together. After the 2025 election, both the LDF and UDF chose to remain in opposition rather than join hands to prevent the BJP from taking control. Their positions have remained sharply divided on several political issues, and the LDF’s refusal to support the UDF’s earlier no-confidence initiative showed the difficulty of stitching together an anti-BJP arrangement at the corporation level. The resignation could nevertheless force both fronts to reconsider their approach. A no-confidence motion, if brought, would require the prescribed number of councillors to move it, while its success would depend on the numbers at the council. With the NDA reduced to 50, the BJP can no longer rely on the comfortable arithmetic it had at the beginning of its term. The independent councillor’s position could also assume greater significance. For the BJP, therefore, the immediate strategy is likely to be two-fold: retain the support that keeps the administration afloat and fight the Sasthamangalam by-election with the aim of restoring the lost seat. For the LDF and UDF, the dilemma is different. They now have an opportunity to challenge the BJP’s hold, but doing so would require an understanding between two fronts that have so far remained unwilling to share the same political platform in the corporation. The numbers have changed. Whether the political equations change with them remains the bigger question. Also Read: BJP’s R Sreelekha criticises party for backing out of its promise The BJP was well aware of Sreelekha’s displeasure, but it apparently did not see this move coming. The immediate challenge before the leadership is to prevent an internal disagreement from turning into a larger political embarrassment. Sreelekha had entered the Corporation election with the expectation that a BJP victory would put her in contention for the Mayor’s post. The party, however, settled on Rajesh for the position after emerging as the single largest bloc by a narrow margin. The decision did not go down well with Sreelekha, who made her dissatisfaction known within the party as well as in public. The leadership subsequently appeared to have explored the possibility of accommodating her with a position at the national level. A berth in the National Commission for Women was understood to be among the possibilities discussed. The recent appointment of Nivedita Subramanian, who had contested the Guruvayur Assembly constituency in 2016, to the National Commission for Women has added another layer to the episode. The party is now scrambling to contain the fallout. State BJP president Rajeev Chandrasekhar is expected to hold a direct discussion with Sreelekha in an effort to persuade her to withdraw the resignation. The differences themselves were hardly a secret within the BJP. What appears to have caught the leadership off guard was Sreelekha’s decision to take the dispute out of the party forum and announce an exit. For the BJP, it is an awkward move on a political chessboard where every piece matters. What began as a disagreement over the Mayor’s chair has now left the party having to work out its next move in the Corporation. title: GS Yuasa stock reports 7.5 percent revenue growth - AD HOC NEWS
content: GS Yuasa stock was last at JPY 5,448 on October 2, while Q1 operating profit reached JPY 11.6 billion. Analysts set a JPY 7,000 consensus target. GS Yuasa (ISIN JP3385820000) reported Q1 2026 revenue of JPY 141.7 billion, up 7.5 percent from JPY 131.9 billion a year earlier. The battery maker's operating profit rose 39.3 percent to JPY 11.6 billion, giving the stock a fundamentals-led story as the second quarter approaches. According to MarketScreener on September 21, 2026, Q1 revenue growth came from higher overseas lead-acid battery volumes and stronger hybrid-vehicle lithium-ion shipments. Operating margin widened to 8.2 percent from 6.3 percent in Q1 2025, while net profit increased 15.7 percent to JPY 7.6 billion from JPY 6.5 billion. The mix matters. Pricing corrections and a more profitable sales mix offset higher labor, logistics, depreciation and raw-material costs, according to MarketScreener. For investors, the 1.9 percentage-point margin improvement is a more important operating signal than revenue growth alone. The analyst picture remains constructive but leaves room for disagreement. Investing.com lists a Buy consensus from 9 analysts, including 8 Buy ratings, 1 Hold and 0 Sell ratings. The average 12-month target is JPY 7,000, with a high of JPY 8,200 and a low of JPY 5,300. That target is 28.5 percent above the October 2 price of JPY 5,448. The comparison also shows the market's higher expectations: the current price sits 31.0 percent below the 52-week high of JPY 7,899, despite the company's stronger Q1 margin. GS Yuasa priced JPY 10.0 billion of green bonds on September 4, 2026, with a 3.443 percent annual coupon and a 10-year maturity, according to MarketScreener. The company said the proceeds are intended for storage-battery projects and renewable-energy facilities. The next scheduled checkpoint is November 6, 2026, when GS Yuasa plans to announce results for the six months ended September 30, 2026, followed by a briefing, per the GS Yuasa investor-relations calendar. That report will show whether the Q1 margin improvement is extending into the first half. GS Yuasa stock was last at JPY 5,448 on the Tokyo Stock Exchange on October 2, 2026 at 3:30 p.m. JST, down 0.95 percent on the session. title: From 'Coffee Prince' to 'My Lovely Sam Soon,' 2000s K-drama fashion is back - The Korea Times
content: Young Korean women are embracing a grown woman look, a more sophisticated and understated fashion trend, as brands shift fall and winter collections away from Y2K-style boldness. The aesthetic is also reviving interest in 2000s K-drama wardrobes from Coffee Prince, My Lovely Sam Soon and High Kick Through the Roof. Sales data and brand moves suggest the trend is already spreading beyond social media. GS Shop, the home-shopping unit of GS Retail, unveils knitwear and jackets made with 100 percent wool from its fashion brand So Natural on Sept. 23. For the fall and winter season, the brand focuses on premium materials and natural silhouettes. Courtesy of GS Shop After years of playful, edgy Y2K fashion dominating wardrobes, young Korean women are turning toward something decidedly more grown-up. The so-called "grown woman look," a Korean fashion trend centered on sophisticated, understated femininity, is gaining traction among women in their 20s and 30s. Fashion brands are responding with fall and winter collections built around polished silhouettes, richer colors and restrained styling. According to the fashion industry, the trend marks a shift away from the bold, youthful aesthetic associated with the Y2K revival. Instead, consumers are gravitating toward looks that appear effortless yet refined, with a relaxed and restrained mood. Deep colors, subtle femininity and clean silhouettes are among the defining elements. Female characters from TV dramas that aired about 20 years ago appear in Instagram search results for the Korean term "grown woman." Screenshot from Instagram The trend has even revived interest in the wardrobes of female characters from Korean TV shows that aired nearly two decades ago. On social media and in online communities, fashions worn by Han Yoo-joo, played by Chae Jung-an in the 2007 drama "Coffee Prince;" Yoo Hee-jin, played by Jung Ryeo-won in the 2005 series "My Lovely Sam Soon;" and Yoo In-na's character in the 2009 sitcom "High Kick Through the Roof" are being rediscovered as inspiration. Sales data suggest the trend is moving beyond online buzz. W Concept, an online fashion platform operated by Shinsegae Group, found that transactions for fall clothing increased more than 30 percent from Aug. 23 to 28 compared with Aug. 18 to 22. Knitwear sales jumped 85 percent, followed by mid-heeled shoes at 40 percent, tote bags at 35 percent and outerwear at 20 percent — all categories closely associated with the grown woman look. Red, burgundy and plum have also emerged as popular accent colors. LeMouton's Let's Mary Jane sneakers, launched in October last year, reached cumulative sales of 100,000 pairs within a year. Courtesy of LeMouton Casual footwear brand LeMouton has joined the trend with Mary Jane-style sneakers. Characterized by a rounded toe and a strap across the top of the foot, Mary Janes have become a natural fit for consumers seeking a feminine look without excessive embellishment. Sales of LeMouton's Mary Jane lineup reached 11 billion won ($7.8 million) through August, up 110 percent from the same period last year. GS Shop, the home-shopping business operated by GS Retail, is also targeting demand for the grown woman aesthetic. Its fashion label So Natural has chosen "soft minimalism" as its fall and winter concept, emphasizing luxurious textures including cashmere, wool and camel hair. "This fall, fashion that highlights the appeal of the material and silhouette itself rather than elaborate decoration is drawing attention, and products using cashmere and wool are proving popular," a GS Shop official said. Women's contemporary fashion brand Instantfunk reinterprets its signature aesthetic through a contemporary lens for its fall and winter collection under the concept "NEXT CHAPTER." Courtesy of Instantfunk Vintage-inspired casual brands are also embracing the shift. Women's contemporary fashion brand Instantfunk is using familiar pieces such as denim and knitwear in its fall and winter collection, pairing them with belts and accessories for a more polished aesthetic. "While maintaining the brand's existing identity, we added voluminous silhouettes, contrasting materials and accessory accents in line with the popularity of the grown woman look," an Instantfunk official said. "We are proposing a more refined and expanded style." The growing appeal of the aesthetic reflects a broader change in fashion tastes among younger Korean consumers: After seasons of crop tops, playful nostalgia and Y2K experimentation, understated sophistication is having its moment. title: McAleer: “Choosing the Battles” Gave AutoTechnic GS Title - Sportscar365
content: Stevan McAleer on taking measured approach to Pilot Challenge GS title… Stevan McAleer credited the mindset of “choosing the battles” that allowed he and Austin Krainz to secure the IMSA Michelin Pilot Challenge GS title at Michelin Raceway Road Atlanta. McAleer and Krainz drove their No. 27 AutoTechnic Racing BMW M4 GT4 EVO to a third place finish in Friday’s Fox Factory 120, which helped BMW earn its eighth manufacturers’ championship in series competition. McAleer took control of the points lead for good after a multi-car battle following the second round of pitstops. He said the mindset of thinking big picture and knowing the points scenario before he took over driving duties from Krainz paid dividends in the second half of the race. “I know I’ve already worked out the points [of] where I need to be in what position I need to be in,” he told Sportscar365. “I’m just choosing the battles and making sure that you know we don’t go off the race track for no reason. “Just before I got in, they showed me that we were all tied on points at 2400 apiece. That’s not good because the 95 car had had a win under the belt, so they would have taken it. “The mindset is really to try and do everything we’ve done all season. Don’t mess up the pit stop, nice driver change, which we did, and a really good out and in lap. “Again, I don’t think I had a strong in-lap on the first stop, but I really nailed the second one. The racing changes so much.” McAleer battled the No. 95 Turner Motorsport BMW and the No. 13 McCumbee McAleer Racing Ford Mustang GT4 both on-track and for the title. Recalling the final hour battle, McAleer said he needed balance between execution and aggressiveness. “I think again a lot of faster cars out there, but just execution and a lot of my moves were aggressive today,” he said. “But I had to force the issue to try and get by, and a couple of cars made some side to side contact, but much racing. “The race was a lot of fun. We knew what we had to do. “When you get to this stage in the championship, there’s cars that I’ll race and there’s cars that I will not race. We had to race the No. 95 and the No. 13. “We knew that the 44 car [Ibiza Farm Motorsport McLaren Artura GT4] was going to be as fast as can be, and it was to get as close to that car as we could, so the team executed perfectly. “Aside from that, a special moment for Austin and Roland [Krainz]. I could see them crying on the wall there, so it was a special moment.” McAleer won his second Pilot Challenge title after taking the 2015 championship with CJ Wilson Racing in a Mazda MX-5 in the now-defunct ST class. He said being on both slides of a title fight in the series helped him focus in the final stint. “I just put my head down and hit my marks,” said McAleer. “I’ve been in this position before, both as a winner and a loser. “We had a mechanical failure in 2016 that took another championship. Those last 20 minutes of the race, you can hear every nut and bolt creak on that car. “I honestly thought we would have would have been quite a ways off to some of the other manufacturers, but we had pace. “We’re real quick in the corners, good in breaking. We lacked a little bit in straight line speed, but we could make the rest of that up in the corners, so it was a good day.” Jack Rachinsky is a contributor to Sportscar365.com. title: RU Shibir cancelled Rucsu GS Ammar's 'Sathi' membership last year, expelled over allegations of post trading - The Business Standard
content: Rajshahi University Central Students' Union (Rucsu) General Secretary Salahuddin Ammar was a "Sathi" of Bangladesh Islami Chhatra Shibir and had his status cancelled last year after failing to adequately respond to allegations including financial irregularities and the trading of positions in the metropolitan Chhatra Shakti unit. According to a letter issued by RU Shibir unit on 31 July, Shibir's monthly secretariat meeting in February 2025 decided to suspend Ammar's "Sathi" membership over allegations of moral misconduct, neglect of basic religious duties, freely mixing with women, illegal financial transactions and involvement in activities contrary to the organisation's aims and objectives. The letter said the September 2025 monthly secretariat meeting later decided to cancel his "Sathi" membership after he failed to adequately respond to the allegations. The letter also expressed concern that Ammar's activities and alleged involvement in "criminal activities" could create instability on campus. It said his "provocative activities" could also push the university towards conflict. Signed by Shibir's RU unit President Mujahid Faisal, the letter instructed Shibir leaders to stop communicating with Ammar. It also instructed activists to avoid Ammar in their online and offline activities and refrain from making any negative comments or reactions about him. It also urged elected Rucsu office-bearers not to maintain organisational ties with Ammar and asked Shibir activists at all levels to sever contact with him. Ahmed Munshi, sports secretary of the unit's 2025 committee, and two other leaders of its current committee confirmed the authenticity of the letter to The Business Standard today (30 September). A Shibir leader, speaking on condition of anonymity, said an investigation committee had been formed to look into various allegations against Ammar, including the theft of laptops from a city corporation building, trading in positions in the metropolitan Chhatra Shakti unit and financial irregularities. Asked about Ammar's political background, the leader said Ammar had originally been a "Sathi" of Shibir's Tamirul Millat Madrasah unit and worked with Alternative Literature - a cultural organisation at Rajshahi University. The leader claimed that the organisation was primarily run by Shibir members and that Ammar had been formally involved with Shibir until after the July Uprising in 2024. Another Shibir leader, also speaking on condition of anonymity, said the organisation initially suspended Ammar's membership under its rules and sought his response to the allegations. The decision to cancel his membership was taken after he failed to adequately respond, the leader said. The latest letter was issued after further alleged irregularities were observed and amid concerns over Ammar's conduct, the leader added. Previously, Ammar has repeatedly denied having any affiliation with Shibir. He was elected Rucsu general secretary from the "Anti-Dominance Unity" panel, which was widely discussed as a "dummy panel" of Shibir during the 2025 Rucsu election. He later drew controversy over several campus incidents, including multiple mob incidents, alleged irregularities in financial transactions involving Rucsu funds and incidents in which students were beaten. During that time, Shibir's RU unit said at a press conference that it would not take responsibility for Ammar. This reporter made several attempts to contact Ammar for comment, but received no response. title: BMW F 450 R: Four variants, prices and differences from the GS - motorcycles.news
content:
After the F 450 GS adventure tourer, BMW Motorrad’s new twin-cylinder engine gets its second home. The F 450 R has been developed as a standalone naked bike, but uses the GS’s engine, frame and swingarm as its basis. It is part of the new arrivals for the 2027 model year and, according to BMW, is not only aimed at riders with an A2 licence. The manufacturer also has returning riders and experienced motorcyclists in mind who are looking for a light bike for town and country roads. The price stands out in particular: at 6,490 euros (around 7,285 US dollars), the base model undercuts the Aprilia Tuono 457. In Germany, the BMW F 450 R costs between 6,490 euros (around 7,285 US dollars) and 7,220 euros (around 8,104 US dollars). The price difference comes down to the equipment and paintwork of the four variants. The base model is only available in Cosmic Black. Even this version comes with three riding modes, ABS Pro, traction control, a 6.5-inch TFT display and heated grips. What it lacks is the shift assistant. The F 450 R Exclusive is also black and costs 6,770 euros (around 7,599 US dollars). For an extra 280 euros, it adds Shift Assistant Pro and the so-called sport suspension, with a fork adjustable for rebound and compression damping. Anyone who wants a different colour has to go for the F 450 R M Sport. It costs 6,920 euros (around 7,768 US dollars) and is painted in Snaefell White / M Motorsport. This includes a white frame and rim stickers in the M colours. Alongside Shift Assistant Pro and sport suspension, Riding Modes Pro is also standard here. The fourth variant is the M Sport with Innovation Package for 7,220 euros (around 8,104 US dollars). It additionally comes with the Easy Ride Clutch. For comparison: the Aprilia Tuono 457 starts at 6,700 euros (around 7,521 US dollars). The most expensive F 450 R costs as much as the F 450 GS in its basic version. In the UK, the F 450 R is available from 6,395 pounds (around 7,521 euros / 8,442 US dollars). There are no plans for the USA yet, however. A BMW spokesperson said: “There are no current plans to bring the 2027 F 450 R to the US. The F 450 R may be introduced to the U.S. at a later date.” The F 450 R uses the liquid-cooled 420 cc parallel twin from the F 450 GS. It produces 48 hp (35 kW) at 8,750 rpm and delivers 43 Nm (32 lb-ft) at 6,750 rpm. For the naked bike, BMW has retuned the engine for road use. This does not change the performance figures. According to BMW, 80 per cent of maximum torque is already available at 3,000 rpm. So the engine does not have to be revved hard all the time to make brisk progress. The key data in detail: bore is 72 mm and stroke 51.6 mm. Two overhead camshafts operate four valves per cylinder via lightweight finger followers. The intake valves have a head diameter of 29 mm, the exhaust valves 24.3 mm. The compression ratio is 13:1. Port fuel injection with the BMS-Z engine management system prepares the mixture. The throttle is electronic: a sensor on the twistgrip reports the rider’s input to the engine management, which then opens the 38 mm throttle bodies. One special feature is the crankshaft. Its crankpins are offset by 135 degrees, which BMW says is unique on the motorcycle market. This results in an uneven firing interval and a distinctive sound. A balancer shaft in front of the crankshaft counters vibrations. To save weight, the clutch and transmission covers are made of magnesium. The stainless steel silencer sits under the engine and contains two catalytic converters. According to BMW, this solution saves around two kilograms. It is also meant to offer more lean angle and reduce the risk of the passenger or luggage being burned by a hot exhaust. BMW quotes fuel consumption of 3.8 litres per 100 kilometres according to the WMTC standard. With the 14-litre tank, this gives a theoretical range of up to 368 kilometres. The engine meets the Euro 5+ emissions standard and runs on premium unleaded. The F 450 R is said to accelerate from 0 to 100 km/h in 5.7 seconds, with a top speed of 169 km/h. A six-speed gearbox transmits power to an X-ring chain on the left-hand side. Servicing is due every 10,000 kilometres. The Easy Ride Clutch is a centrifugal clutch that engages and disengages automatically depending on engine speed. To pull away, you simply open the throttle; when stopping, the clutch disengages by itself. A centrifugal clutch uses the outward force that builds as engine speed rises to close the clutch. Unlike many conventional systems, the BMW’s clutch stays closed on the overrun. Engine braking therefore works until just before the bike comes to a standstill. The clutch only opens once the engine reaches idle speed. This is meant to make it practically impossible to stall the engine. The clutch lever still remains on the handlebar. Anyone who prefers to modulate it themselves when manoeuvring or on twisty roads can use the clutch conventionally at any time. From the factory, the Easy Ride Clutch is only available on the M Sport as part of the Innovation Package. On the other variants, it can be retrofitted as Original BMW Motorrad Accessories. It adds one kilogram to the weight. Only in combination with Shift Assistant Pro can the F 450 R be ridden entirely without touching the clutch. The shift assistant allows clutchless upshifts and downshifts and therefore almost no interruption in drive. According to BMW, this also significantly reduces the head nodding of rider and passenger when changing gear. The shift assistant is standard on the Exclusive and M Sport and can be retrofitted to the base model. For track riding, the shift pattern can also be reversed with little effort. The F 450 R adopts the steel frame and aluminium swingarm of the F 450 GS, but its geometry, suspension, wheels and ergonomics are designed entirely for the road. Instead of an adventure look, the focus is on short distances and quick turn-in. Marc Weber, Lead Engineer Complete Vehicle for the F 450 R, puts it this way: “With the BMW F 450 R, we have consistently transferred the technical basis of the F 450 GS into a standalone BMW naked bike.” Chassis geometry, seating position and the entire package were retailored to the demands of the road. The trellis frame is made from welded steel tubes and forged parts, with the engine integrated as a load-bearing element. The wheelbase is 1,405 mm, the steering head angle 23.4 degrees and the trail 110 mm. At the front, a KYB upside-down fork with 43 mm inner tubes, gold-coloured stanchions and a forged aluminium triple clamp does the work. At the rear, a hollow-cast aluminium double-sided swingarm guides the wheel, combined with a directly mounted KYB shock absorber that is adjustable for preload and rebound. Suspension travel is 140 mm at both ends. The F 450 R rolls on 17-inch cast aluminium wheels with 110/70-17 tyres at the front and 150/60-17 at the rear. BMW fits the Eurogrip Protorq Extreme as standard. At the front, a floating 310 mm disc is gripped by a radially mounted Brembo four-piston monobloc caliper. At the rear sits a 240 mm disc with a single-piston floating caliper from ByBre. When it comes to weight, the F 450 R hits a limit set by the A2 regulations. They allow a maximum of 35 kW and a power-to-weight ratio of no more than 0.2 kW per kilogram. A full-power A2 motorcycle must therefore weigh at least 175 kilograms. That is exactly where the F 450 R sits at 175 kg (386 lbs) ready to ride, or 176 kg (388 lbs) with the Easy Ride Clutch. The Aprilia Tuono 457 achieves the same figures, but takes the opposite approach: its frame is aluminium and its swingarm steel. The BMW’s permissible total weight is 355 kg (783 lbs). All variants come as standard with the Rain, Road and Dynamic riding modes as well as ABS Pro, Dynamic Brake Control, Dynamic Traction Control and engine drag torque control. Added to this are a 6.5-inch TFT display, LED lighting, a USB-C socket and three-stage heated grips. The riding modes change throttle response and the control systems. Rain is intended for wet roads, with soft throttle response and a focus on stability. Road is designed for dry roads and a balanced set-up. In Dynamic, traction control, wheelie detection and engine drag torque control intervene later. Engine drag torque control prevents the rear wheel from locking when closing the throttle abruptly or downshifting. ABS Pro also works when leaned over and is meant to prevent the bike from standing up during panic braking in corners. Dynamic Brake Control detects when the rider accidentally opens the throttle during hard braking and keeps the throttle valves closed. The dynamic brake light warns following traffic of hard braking in two stages. Riding Modes Pro adds the Dynamic Pro mode, in which throttle response, ABS and traction control can be adjusted individually. The package is standard on the M Sport variants and available as an accessory for the base and Exclusive models. On the M Sport variants, the display then shows three additional Sport Screens with information on traction control, braking force and lean angle, as well as a lap timer. The TFT is operated via the Multi-Controller on the left handlebar end. Smartphone and helmet communication system can be paired via Bluetooth for phone calls or music, with no app required. Depending on the market, the free BMW Motorrad Connected app also shows arrow navigation on the display. Anyone wanting map navigation needs the navigation preparation available as an accessory, together with the ConnectedRide Navigator or ConnectedRide Smartphone Cradle. Visually, the F 450 R takes its cue from the S 1000 R with the “tail up, nose down” principle: the front sits low and the tail is raised high. The side panels form a stylised R, and the LED headlight features the bracket-shaped daytime running light of BMW’s naked bikes. Alexander Buckan, Head of Design at BMW Motorrad, says: “With its striking side panel and the naked-bike-typical flyline following the tail up – nose down principle, the BMW F 450 R unmistakably yet subtly quotes the design DNA of the S 1000 R without copying it one-to-one.” For the seating position, BMW relies on a high, 76 cm wide aluminium handlebar placed close to the rider. The two-piece standard seat is 790 mm high, and the inside leg curve measures 1,770 mm. A low accessory seat lowers the height to 775 mm, while a high sport seat raises it to 810 mm. Brake and clutch levers are adjustable as standard. The gear lever, footbrake lever and side stand are made of forged aluminium, and the passenger footrest brackets are bolted to the rear frame. Overall, the F 450 R is 2,002 mm long and 825 mm wide across the handlebar ends. BMW is offering a dedicated accessories range for the F 450 R from launch. According to BMW, deliveries of the naked bike are expected to start in June 2027. For everyday use and short trips, there are soft cases with 16.5 litres of capacity each including holders, a 5 to 8 litre tank bag that attaches directly to the fuel filler cap without straps, plus luggage rolls and tail bags in several sizes. A gold aluminium handlebar and black bar-end mirrors add visual accents. For protection, BMW offers engine protection bars, a radiator guard, hand guards, axle and engine protectors and M lever protectors. Depending on the variant, the Easy Ride Clutch, Shift Assistant Pro and Riding Modes Pro can also be retrofitted as accessories. In Germany, the BMW F 450 R costs from 6,490 euros (around 7,285 US dollars). The Exclusive is priced at 6,770 euros, the M Sport at 6,920 euros and the M Sport with Innovation Package at 7,220 euros (around 8,104 US dollars). According to BMW, the F 450 R is expected to be available in Germany from June 2027. There are currently no plans for the USA. Yes, with 48 hp (35 kW) the F 450 R is designed for the European A2 licence category. No restriction is needed, as it does not exceed the permitted maximum output from the factory. The BMW F 450 R weighs 175 kg (386 lbs) ready to ride. With the optional Easy Ride Clutch, it weighs 176 kg (388 lbs). The F 450 R’s standard seat is 790 mm high. Accessory seats can lower it to 775 mm or raise it to 810 mm. ➜ This article is part of our comprehensive overview: New Motorcycles 2027: All Models, Releases and Highlights at a Glance. title: Circle H Wins; AutoTechnic Takes GS Title at Road Atlanta - Sportscar365
content: Thomas Merrill, Martin Sarukhanyan hold on to win Fox Factory 120… Thomas Merrill and Martin Sarukhanyan claimed Circle H Racing’s first IMSA Michelin Pilot Challenge victory in Friday’s Fox Factory 120, while AutoTechnic Racing’s Austin Krainz and Stevan McAleer secured the GS class championship at Michelin Raceway Road Atlanta. The No. 33 Bryan Herta Autosport Hyundai Elantra N TCR of Bryson Morris and Mason Filippi secured the TCR class title by starting the race. Pole-sitter Jaxon Bell stretched his overall to over seven seconds before their first pit stop handed the No. 23 Toyota GR Supra GT4 EVO2 to Ford Koch. The race ran green to the end of the first stint. The No. 66 YRB Aston Martin Vantage GT4 Evo received a drive-through penalty for incident responsibility with the title-contending No. 27 AutoTechnic Racing BMW M4. YRB had another drive-through for contact with the No. 61 McCumbee McAleer Racing Ford Mustang GT4 of Jenson Altzman in the Esses. Debris in Turn 7 brought out the first full course yellow near the end of the pit sequence. Koch cycled to the front with championship contenders Michael Cooper and Robert Noaker rounding out the top three in GS at the restart. Filippi led TCR once the action resumed. The pole-sitting No. 93 MMG Honda Civic FL5 TCR, now piloted by LP Montour, restarted in fourth after the pit stops. The No. 44 Ibiza Farm Motorsport McLaren Artura GT4 of Cooper kept Koch honest after the restart. The McLaren pitted with 48 minutes to go chasing the Toyota by less than half a second. With 44 minutes left, Cooper muscled Koch out of Turn 10b to take the effective lead during the second pit cycle. The No. 26 Heart of Racing Team Aston Martin of Hannah Grisham passed Noaker out of the pits to take third. Koch had to retire from second place. Grisham then maneuvered around Mike Skeen in the No. 60 KohR Motorsports Ford Mustang with 37 minutes left to jump up to the second spot. But both Grisham and Noaker separately ran wide to allow the No. 27 BMW M4 GT4 EVO of McAleer to jump back into the championship lead. Cooper and Ibiza Farm’s title hopes were dashed when the McLaren suffered a steering issue from the lead with 18 minutes to go. Merrill inherited the lead for the team’s first win. The full course yellow came out with under three minutes remaining to end the race. The CarBahn with Peregrine Racing BMW of Jeff Westphal and the No. 93 Honda of Montour collided on the frontstretch after contact by the No. 12 RAFA Racing Toyota of Kiko Porto. The No. 46 Team TGM Mustang GT4 of Matt Plumb and Paul Holton took second in GS. McAleer and Krainz came home in third to clinch the title without winning a race in the season. Filippi held on for the TCR victory on top of the class championship. The No. 21 Victor Gonzalez Racing CUPRA Leon VZ TCR of William Tally and Caleb Bacon finished second with the No. 56 Baker Racing Audi RS 3 LMS TCR of Dean Baker and Kenny Riedmann completed the podium. Jack Rachinsky is a contributor to Sportscar365.com. title: The new 2027 BMW F 450 GS - Motor Sports Newswire
content: WOODCLIFF LAKE, NJ – October 2, 2026 – (Motor Sports NewsWire) – BMW Motorrad USA is proud to announce the new, 2027 BMW F 450 GS. A genuine GS that delivers class leading technology, safety systems, excellent power and torque, and agile handling both on- and off-road – all combining to maximize both short and long-distance riding enjoyment, just as its larger displacement Adventure siblings do. “With the new BMW F 450 GS, BMW Motorrad presents a genuine BMW GS in the 48 hp A2 class. It embodies the essence of a GS: Get on, twist the throttle, have fun – with full control and maximum confidence. Its low weight, superior performance and perfect balance between agility and stability ensure a particularly intuitive riding experience. Thanks to its precise handling and typical GS expertise, it performs impressively both on and off the road. The F 450 GS is the perfect ‘best buddy’ for every riding situation. It is uncomplicated, robust, and always ready. It sets the benchmark for sporty adventure bikes in its class.” Markus Flasch, CEO BMW Motorrad. 420 cc parallel twin with balance shaft and 135-degree crankpin offset. “With the BMW GS-typical flyline, the recognizable radiator grille, signature lighting, and sleek rear end, the design language of the new BMW F 450 GS deliberately draws close attention to the iconic design of its big sister, the R 1300 GS. It skillfully transfers its spirit to the 48 hp 400 – 500 cc range. This also includes sophisticated ergonomics for the best possible accessibility and vehicle control.” The new BMW F 450 GS is a completely redesigned, new construction for the 48 hp 400 – 500 cc class. Its design focuses on implementing the current BMW GS design language. With iconic features such as the LED headlight with “X” lighting elements and the distinctive flyline, the bike’s affiliation with the BMW Motorrad GS family is apparent at first glance. The characteristic flyline runs from the front GS “beak,” across the tank and seat, and continues to the very narrow, slim rear. The agility and lightness of the rear section emphasize the dynamic character of the new BMW F 450 GS. Optimum ergonomics for both relaxed and dynamic on- and off-road riding. In terms of both drivetrain and chassis, the new BMW F 450 GS offers everything you would expect from a GS. The ideal riding position in all conditions is ensured by an ergonomic triangle that was developed over countless miles of testing in a wide variety of conditions. The handlebars, made of butted aluminum, are positioned high and close to the body. The body and the 3.6-gallon fuel tank underneath are designed to provide optimal support and a good knee fit when sitting or riding off-road in a standing position. Touring and everyday usability thanks to weather protection and a comprehensive storage space concept. The modular design of the available optional windshields allows for customization. Depending on the intended use and personal preferences, customers can choose the high Tour windshield (height-adjustable) or the clear Rallye windshield. This allows the comfort and protective effect of the new BMW F 450 GS to be tailored to individual requirements. In the event of a fall or crash, Original BMW Motorrad Accessories effectively protect the motorcycle from damage with engine guard, engine protection bars, front axle protectors, and other protective components. The wide range of storage accessories – whether side bags, rear bags, luggage rolls, tank bags, luggage racks or top cases – offers maximum flexibility for almost every application. Three different seat variants, adjustable handlebar levers, handlebar risers and sure-footed foot pegs with adjustable gearshift lever and footbrake lever for optimum riding on- and off-road. The new BMW F 450 GS comes with a two-piece seat (33.3-inch) as standard. With its flat, straight design, it provides an ideal ergonomic position for comfort and dynamics for most riders. The low black rider’s seat (32.7 inches) and the high Rallye seat in Black/White/Red (34.0 inches), available as part of the Original BMW Motorrad Accessories, can be adapted to individual needs. The standard adjustable handlebar levers and the optional accessory 0.79-inch handlebar risers in silver offer further customization options. The new BMW F 450 GS in the GS Trophy Variant comes standard with wider enduro footrests. While primarily designed for on-road use, their serrated profile also makes them suitable for off-road use. The enduro footrests offer an optimal balance between grip and comfort. A very practical feature is the height-adjustable footbrake lever. Using a tool, it can be adjusted vertically by 0.79-inch to two positions to suit individual on- and off-road riding needs. The gearshift lever is also height-adjustable – via a toothed mechanism on the shift shaft. “With its new two-cylinder inline engine, the new BMW F 450 GS boasts an outstanding powertrain for dynamic riding pleasure on- and off-road. Low weight, ample torque, and exceptional smoothness thanks to the unique 135-degree crankpin offset make it a perfect partner for a wide range of applications typical of a GS. With our new Easy Ride Clutch (ERC), the new F 450 GS also offers a significant increase in operating comfort and dynamic performance.” Johann Simon, Project Manager BMW F 450 GS Completely redesigned, smooth-running and distinctive two-cylinder in-line engine for dynamic riding fun on asphalt and for off-road use. For decades, BMW’s F Series GS models have stood for premium offerings in their respective mid-range segments. Their all-around qualities, paragon of riding fun on asphalt roads, and easy and safe handling on off-road terrain have always characterized them. With the F 450 GS, BMW Motorrad is bringing this successful formula to the market in a completely redesigned form for the popular 400 – 500 cc class. It provides optimum riding fun on all types of terrain, whether on asphalt roads or off-road. At the heart of the new BMW F 450 GS is a completely redesigned two-cylinder in-line engine. The main development goals were to build a lightweight, powerful, high-torque, and smooth-running engine. Additionally, during the development of the new engine, particular emphasis was placed on achieving low fuel consumption values and a distinctive sound. The 420 cc displacement results from a 72 mm bore and a 51.6 mm stroke. The new F 450 GS delivers powerful performance and pulling power with a power output of 48 hp at 8,750 rpm and a maximum torque of 32 lb.-ft at 6,750 rpm. Characterful and emotional sound thanks to a crankshaft with a 135-degree crankpin offset and uneven ignition interval. The new BMW F 450 GS’s two-cylinder, in-line, liquid-cooled engine is installed transversely. Unique on the motorcycle market, it features a crankshaft with crankpins offset by 135 degrees. This design is accompanied by a strong emotional character, while at the same time a very low vibration level for the rider. Optimized smooth running is achieved thanks to a counter-rotating counterbalance shaft and wet-sump lubrication. The engine of the new BMW F 450 GS has a counterweight shaft (counterbalance shaft) positioned in front of the crankshaft that absorbs unwanted vibrations. It is driven by a spur gear. In conjunction with the 135-degree offset of the crankshaft, this results in smooth operation. A wet-sump lubrication system with a chain-driven oil pump ensures a reliable oil supply under all operating conditions. The new F 450 GS has an engine guard, which is standard on the GS Trophy, to protect the oil pan from damage during off-road use. Two overhead camshafts, four valves per cylinder operated by rocker arms. Two overhead camshafts rotate in the cylinder head of the new F 450 GS, actuating four valves-per-cylinder via lightweight rocker arms. The timing chain is driven on the right side of the engine by a toothed chain from the crankshaft to the exhaust camshaft. The intake camshaft is driven by a pair of gears via the exhaust camshaft. The valve angles are sized for an optimal combustion chamber design to provide the best possible power, torque, and efficiency. The valve angle is 12 degrees on the intake side and 12.4 degrees on the exhaust side. The valves have a valve head diameter of 29 mm (intake) and 24.3 mm (exhaust). The compression ratio is 13.0:1. An intake manifold fuel injection system with the latest BMS-Z engine management technology is responsible for the air-fuel mixture. An E-Gas system sends the rider’s request directly from the throttle grip sensor to the engine control unit. This unit regulates the opening angle of the throttle valves for optimal controllability and response. Easy Ride Clutch (ERC) for a significant increase in operating and riding comfort. A special technical highlight of the new BMW F 450 GS is the Easy Ride Clutch (ERC). This innovative system is standard on the GS Trophy variant or available as an optional accessory. In combination with the BMW Gear Shift Assist Pro, manual operation of the clutch lever is completely eliminated – from starting off to gear changes to demanding maneuvers. The clutch lever, however, remains installed. This allows the rider to use the clutch manually when needed – a decisive advantage in special riding situations, for example, to lift the front wheel over an obstacle or to improve control when descending on slippery surfaces. The heart of the ERC is a centrifugal unit in the clutch, which engages the clutch depending on the engine speed. The handling is similar to that of a conventional clutch operation: Starting off is achieved simply by opening the throttle with a gear engaged. If a gear that’s too high is selected, a corresponding warning appears on the display. In heavy city traffic, on tight bends, or off-road, the ERC provides noticeable relief for the rider, as it effectively prevents the engine from stalling. Technologically, it is a particularly advanced form of the centrifugal clutch. Unlike conventional systems, it remains closed during overrun. The result is familiar and predictable handling, equivalent to that of a conventional clutch. The clutch can be used as usual at any time while riding, if necessary. Engine braking is fully maintained until the vehicle is almost at a standstill; only when the idle speed is reached does the clutch automatically open – just as the rider would otherwise do manually. Even when rolling with the vehicle in gear, for example when riding downhill, the engine is actively dragged along, generating effective engine braking torque. The clutch remains closed during overrun, ensuring maximum control. At the same time, the rider can intervene at any time using the clutch lever and manually override the system. The ERC thus enables confident handling even in complex driving situations – whether maneuvering, in city traffic, on winding roads, or off-road – and elevates driving dynamics and comfort to a new level. Six-speed transmission with optional Gear Shift Assist Pro for fast upshifts and downshifts without the need to use the clutch. To optimize riding dynamics, the redesigned six-speed transmission transmits torque to the left-hand secondary drive via an X-ring chain. For fast upshifts and downshifts without clutch operation, the new F 450 GS is offered with the Gear Shift Assist Pro in the Sport and GS Trophy variants. It allows the rider to shift up without using the clutch, providing perfect acceleration with virtually no interruption in traction. Additionally, Gear Shift Assist Pro, standard on Sport and GS Trophy variants, allows for downshifts without using the clutch. This feature enables very fast gear changes, minimizes clutch actuation, and significantly reduces undesirable influences on the rear wheel and jerking movements caused by load changes. Gear Shift Assist Pro also significantly reduces the independent movements of the rider and passenger during conventional gear changes, making shared motorcycle enjoyment even more comfortable. Right-hand high-quality stainless steel exhaust system. The exhaust system of the new BMW F 450 GS is made entirely of stainless steel and is equipped with two catalytic converters for emission control. Mounting on the right-hand side of the vehicle is particularly advantageous when pushing the motorcycles – usually from the left-hand side. The muffler, which is also on the right, provides the necessary clearance and reduces the risk of getting burnt on the hot muffler. Standard riding modes “Rain”, “Road” and “Enduro” as well as ABS, DBC, DTC and Engine Drag Torque control provide a high degree of riding fun and safety. “Enduro Pro” Riding Mode part of Sport and GS Trophy variants. The new BMW F 450 GS offers three standard riding modes: “Rain”, “Road” and “Enduro”, allowing the motorcycle to be adapted to suit individual preferences. Standard equipment also includes ABS Pro, DBC, Dynamic Traction Control (DTC) as well as Engine Drag Torque control (MSR). The “Rain”, “Road” and “Enduro” riding modes are intelligently linked to the control systems and allow the new BMW F 450 GS to be adapted specifically to the respective riding conditions. The “Rain” mode is designed for use on wet roads. Throttle response is softer, and all control systems are designed to maximize stability and control. “Road” mode is intended for use on dry roads. The engine’s throttle response is direct, and the traction control remains stable in the mid-range. All other control systems are also designed for maximum stability. The “Enduro” mode is designed for off-road use with standard road tires and provides the same throttle response as the “Rain” mode. Traction control provides maximum stability, while front wheel lift-off detection, engine drag torque control, and dynamic traction control remain minimally active. The additional “Enduro Pro” mode, available as part of the GS Trophy variant, is designed for off-road use with rough terrain tires. Wheelie control and rear wheel ABS are deactivated in this mode. ABS Pro, DTC, and throttle response can be customized in this mode as well. “Our chassis concept for the new BMW F 450 GS is based on a completely redesigned tubular steel frame that integrates the two-cylinder inline engine as a load-bearing element,” explains Marc Weber, engineer for the BMW F 450 GS. “The focus of development was on compact packaging for optimal accessibility, high riding precision, and agile handling on and off-road. The short wheelbase and balanced chassis geometry enabled us to achieve particularly agile yet stable handling.” New chassis with tubular steel frame for optimal rigidity and riding precision. The newly developed chassis of the BMW F 450 GS relies on a welded tubular steel frame with integrated forged parts. This design combines low weight with high strength, thus meeting the demands of both dynamic road riding and demanding off-road passages. The use of steel as a frame material offers advantages over aluminum, especially in tougher terrain. Geometry plays a key role in the vehicle’s dynamic performance: A wheelbase of 57.7 inches, a steering head angle of 28.1 degrees, and a trail of 4.5 inches ensure precise steering response, high stability, and playful handling. At the same time, the compact packaging ensures excellent accessibility to the key components – a plus for both maintenance and tough off-road use. Front KYB upside-down telescopic forks and rear KYB central spring strut featuring progressive damping. BMW GS models always present challenging tasks for chassis developers. In addition to operating on asphalt roads and accommodating a sporty riding style, the requirements of off-road use must also be met. The new BMW F 450 GS is equipped with high-quality KYB spring and damper elements that reflect this diverse range of applications. The result is a responsive chassis that maximizes traction in any riding situation. The front wheel is guided by a rigid 43 mm KYB upside-down telescopic forks. Front suspension travel is 7.1 inches. The “Sport Suspension” is part of the Sport and GS Trophy variants and here, the forks are adjustable for both rebound and compression. The fixed fork tubes are anodized in gold, as are the butted aluminum handlebars. The fork bridge is made from forged aluminum. The rear wheel is guided by a closed, lightweight, hollow cast aluminum, double armed swinging arm with a directly linked, central suspension shock with progressive damping, which is unique in this segment. This damping principle originates from off-road sports. BMW Motorrad has patented this technology as the WAD system and has developed it further. A damping system prevents the spring strut from bottoming out by increasing compression damping with increasing compression. The central KYB spring strut of the new F 450 GS has an adjustable spring base (“spring preload”) and adjustable rebound damping. Rear suspension travel is 7.1 inches. The wheels and tires are tailored to BMW GS applications. Sporty, dynamic cornering on the road as well as off-road adventures are reflected in the choice of wheels. Accordingly, new F 450 GS is fitted with 2.5 x 19-inch front and 3.5 x 17 inch rear alloy wheels with tubeless tires for road and off-road use, sized 100/90-19 at the front and 130/80-17 at the rear. The new wheels are 2.2 lbs. lighter than the wheels equipped on the G 310 GS. Type approval for the F 450 GS permits fitting all common tire types, including enduro tires. The new BMW F 450 GS offers optional lightweight yet strong cross-spoked wheels measuring 2.5 x 19 inches the front and 3.5 x 17 inches the rear. High-performance brake system in conjunction with BMW Motorrad ABS Pro for safer braking, even when leaning in corners. The front wheel of the new BMW F 450 GS features a floating single-disc brake with a Brembo 4-piston fixed caliper and a 310 mm brake disc diameter for efficient, stable deceleration. A single disc brake with 1-piston floating caliper and 240 mm diameter is used on the rear wheel. The new BMW F 450 GS is equipped with BMW Motorrad ABS Pro as standard. ABS Pro offers more safety when braking in turns by enabling ABS-assisted braking when leaning into corners. ABS Pro prevents the wheels from locking even when the brakes are applied quickly and reduces abrupt changes in steering force and thus the bike from returning to the upright position, even during sudden braking. The benefits are increased braking and riding stability combined with the best possible deceleration even when leaning into corners. Depending on the selected riding mode, ABS Pro and the engine drag torque control (MSR) offer adapted control characteristics for optimum braking maneuvers. Dynamic Brake Control (DBC) increases safety when braking, even in difficult situations, by preventing the throttle from being activated unintentionally. As soon as the sensor cluster supplies a certain deceleration value during braking, any simultaneous desire to accelerate on the part of the rider is detected as implausible and throttle valve opening is suppressed. This keeps the motorcycle stable and shortens the braking distance. The new F 450 GS offers comprehensive standard equipment such as LED headlight and turn indicators and a 6.5-inch TFT color display with a wealth of connectivity options. The new BMW F 450 GS features an LED headlight with the iconic “X” lighting signature. Based closely on its big sister, the R 1300 GS, it clearly shows its family affiliation. The turn indicator and control lamps of the new F 450 GS also use LED technology. Connectivity – unrivaled information diversity and functionality in the form of a large, easy to read 6.5-inch TFT display. The new F 450 GS already features a large 6.5-inch TFT color display as standard. The quantity of information, quality of its presentation, and user-friendliness are unrivaled. The display was designed to be large to ensure optimum readability, even under difficult lighting conditions. It is linked to the multi-controller on the left handlebar fitting, allowing for quick, safe, and convenient operation. There is a practical USB-C socket in the handlebar area. It offers screen displays tailored to the BMW GS world: the Pure Ride Screen and the Sport Screen (part of the GS Trophy variant), which provide detailed information on DTC, braking power, and lean angle. It is also possible to make phone calls, listen to music and navigate comfortably while riding. If a smartphone and a BMW Motorrad Communication System are connected via Bluetooth to the TFT screen, for example, the rider can conveniently access media playback and telephone functions. These functions can be used without installing an app. If there is an active Bluetooth connection to a standard smartphone, the rider can listen to music while riding. In addition, the free BMW Motorrad Connected app offers practical turn-by-turn navigation directly via the TFT display. Basic navigation is particularly convenient for everyday rides or short trips without additional equipment. For customers who want more than turn-by-turn navigation, BMW Motorrad offers map navigation with navigation preparation, available as an accessory, either with the BMW Motorrad ConnectedRide Navigator (an Original BMW Motorrad Accessory) or the ConnectedRide Smartphone Cradle (used with the BMW Motorrad Connected App). Both can be controlled via the control wheel on the left (MMC). 420cc 2-cylinder water-cooled engine, Chain drive, E-gas (Ride by Wire), 6-speed transmission with spur gearing, Single disc front brake, ABS Pro, Upside down Kayaba front fork, Rear Kayaba suspension strut with travel dependent damping (WAD), Rear rebound adjustable, DTC Dynamic Traction Control, Rear preload adjustable, Heated grips, 6.5-inch TFT color display with Connectivity, USB-C port, LED headlight, turn indicators and brake light, Comfort turn indicators, Multi-Controller, One key for all locks, Adjustable footbrake lever, Adjustable gear shift lever, Engine skid plate, On-board computer, Adjustable clutch lever, Adjustable handbrake lever, Connectivity, MSR (Dynamic engine brake control), DTC Dynamic traction control-disengageable, Ultimate Care Break-In Service. All 2027 model year BMW motorcycle models include the Ultimate Care Break-In Service, or “600 Mile Service” as standard. This included service further provides BMW customers with a truly premium experience. Time and mileage limits apply – maximum 6 months from the in-service date or maximum 750 miles – whichever comes first. The Sport model adds the below additional equipment. The GS Trophy model adds the below additional equipment. Enduro Package ($800) contains cross-spoked wheels. GS Trophy variant only. In addition to the sales, marketing, and distribution of BMW, MINI, Rolls-Royce, and BMW Motorrad vehicles, BMW Group’s business in the U.S. spans 30 locations in 12 states including BMW Group Financial Services, BMW Manufacturing, Designworks, BMW Technology Office USA, and BMW i Ventures. The company’s U.S. plant in South Carolina is the largest single BMW production facility in the world and the global center of competence for BMW Sports Activity Vehicles. The BMW Group sales organization is represented by a nationwide network of 355 BMW retailers, 147 BMW motorcycle retailers, 105 MINI passenger car dealers, and 37 Rolls-Royce Motor Car dealers. title: AI Is Becoming a Stock Picker’s Market - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Goldman Sachs’ weekly newsletter, offering economic and markets analysis from across the firm. Subscribe now. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. Trading in artificial intelligence (AI) stocks is evolving as investor interest broadens beyond semiconductor makers and companies that benefit from capital expenditures in AI, says Peter Callahan, US Technology, Media, and Telecommunications sector specialist in Goldman Sachs FICC and Equities. On The Markets podcast, he says investors are increasingly focused on companies that help organizations implement the technology and AI agents for commerce. Callahan also discusses how rising interest rates are impacting technology stocks, the growing dispersion among software companies, and his outlook for semiconductor stocks. Chris Hussey: This is The Markets. I'm Chris Hussey, and today is Wednesday, September 30th, and I'm here on the Goldman Sachs trading floor with Pete Callahan, who is our US technology, media, and telecommunications sector specialist within FICC and Equities. Pete, thanks so much for joining us again on The Markets. Chris Hussey: All right. Let's get to it, because we had kind of a meh summer. When you look at the 10 biggest tech stocks, half of them were up, half of them were down. Is the AI trade getting long in the tooth? What are customers telling you? Peter Callahan: Yeah, listen, I think tech and AI story is still intact, but you're right, it's, like, nuanced now, right? There's a lot more dispersion, which could be euphemism for bad market breath, right? But what you're starting to see now is much more of a stock picker's market. We're kind of year three, year four of the AI cycle. There's a lot of things to be excited about. There's also a lot of questions that investors are asking. And so I do think the trend for tech is still higher. I still think earnings growth, valuations, and thematic tailwinds are on its side. But to your point, we can kind of go through these lulls after a really good start to the year, call it Jan through June. We've kind of been in consolidation mode this summer, and I think it's a fair thing as investors sort of wrestle with the handful of AI puts and takes down the stretch of the year. Not to mention, of course, rates and oil and macro, and all of those are parts of the conversation today that were a little bit less so in the first half of this year. Chris Hussey: Yeah, I want to get into the macro, but before we do that let's keep exploring that AI trade for a little bit because is the complexion of the AI trade starting to change now? Originally this was an AI infrastructure trade. It started with the semis. It went into the hyperscalers. Is it now making the move into applications, things like agentic AI? How do you look at it? Peter Callahan: Yeah, it's a good question. I mean, let's just start. We had our big flagship technology conference early in September, and it's kind of hard to walk out of that conference and not feel good about the state of AI and the state of tech. And so I kind of, like, that's the backdrop, and that's a good constructive backdrop. But you're right. For the first couple of years when people said AI, they just said semiconductors, kind of CapEx beta. We want to be picks and shuffles. In the last couple of months, you've really started to see more focus up the stack, some of the scaffolding at the infrastructure software, security software layer. Some of the tools and companies that help organizations adopt and deploy AI, that's what you're starting to see. So yes, agentic commerce is part of it. Cybersecurity's been a piece of that. Some of these data infrastructure stocks have been a piece of that. So, I would say the trade has broadened out. And in some capacity you could say, okay, well, it looks flatter and broader, but I think that broader breadth of the trade you could argue is a good thing, even if it creates a little bit more of a stock pickers rather than a sort of a single thematic narrative underneath of it. Chris Hussey: All right. Terrific, Pete. You mentioned Communicopia and Technology, our big conference that we had in September. Did you hear from a lot of people there that these types of AI implementations are working, and that you're getting those types of productivity improvements that people are looking for? Peter Callahan: Yeah, you are. Listen, there's a bunch of soundbites that are coming out of corporates these days around productivity, sort of new revenue opportunities, things like that. It's just the measuring stick, right? Because we're spending trillions of dollars on CapEx. And so I think the market writ large is getting what they want from a productivity narrative, from a use case narrative, now that's maybe emerging on the consumer side with the rise of these personal assistants. But it's always about the measuring stick of how much is going into the ground versus how much companies are getting on the back end. And so of course, with three Q earnings around the season, we'll get this sort of numerical measuring stick in how companies are benefiting from generative AI. Chris Hussey: Okay, Pete, expand on a little bit on the AI build-out here. What are investors most worried about there? Are they worried that we're going to run out of money and stop doing it? What exactly is the risk that they're focused on? Peter Callahan: Yeah, it's a good question. I think most of it would be more about the linearity of the deployment. And so I think investors believe this theme is a decade long mega trend. And so I think investors feel pretty good about the end point, but the linearity has gotten a little bit more, uh, uncertain, right? And that's a comment on sort of the deployment and the physical sort of standing up of these data centers and turning them on. And so I think that's the part of the conversation that's gotten trickier. And again, not to come back to it, but there's just a lot of noise when you look where the rates market is or the oil market is. and so there's just a lot more considerations that investors have today versus kind of that 2023, 2024 cycle of, of generative AI Chris Hussey: Okay, Pete, enough about AI. Let's move on to the broader tech space. Let's talk about software. That was a group that really got taken out earlier in the year. Had a nice summer though, but the last month it's been under a little bit of pressure. Where does software stand today? Peter Callahan: You're going to catch me using the word nuanced again, dispersion, right? Because part of software is that cybersecurity story, that data infrastructure story, and that's become a really big theme for investors to latch onto, and you can kind of call those inference plays, if you will. The sort of core SaaS and application layer of software, the market's still wrestling with that stuff. That's the market where the market's still trying to figure out product market fit and pricing and where they sit alongside that new model layer that's emerged over the last couple of years. And so, it's really kind of a dispersion trade within software, but that's a lot better. I mean, the first half of this year was kind of correlation one type of price action, and that's not great for anybody. And so, it's nice to see dispersion. You're starting to see stock picking come back to software. But the trend has been higher. The group's treated much better over the last couple of months and I still think positioning's a tailwind in that subsector. Chris Hussey: So, if you're a software company that can help implement AI or keep AI safe, you're in good shape. But if you're a software company that has to use AI in order to make their software better, not so yet. Peter Callahan: Yeah or deliver that end product to the customer. That's where the market's trying to figure out how that story plays out over the next couple of months and quarters. Chris Hussey: Okay, let's cut the macro. Tech and rates have always been closely correlated. What's going on today? Peter Callahan: Yeah. Listen, rates have definitely become part of the conversation and a consideration for tech investors. This year you've seen NASDAQ multiple compress about 20%. Now, there's a lot of things that drive that, but I think certainly rates is a piece of that. We now have 10-year yields certainly north of five and a quarter, right? So I think that's been a piece of this story. Now, tech still generated great returns this year, and why is that? That's because the theme is intact, and the earnings growth is intact. And so we look at rates, and we're obviously careful if you sort of lose the long end of the curve. But from a, is it keeping people out of tech? No. But is it putting more pressure on earnings to do the heavy lifting rather than multiple? Certainly, and I think we've seen that this year. Chris Hussey: Now, you mentioned this about the earnings and the PE multiples having come in. Is that a symptom of healthy skepticism in the marketplace around earnings, that people just don't, they don't think the earnings are going to be as strong as we think? Peter Callahan: Yeah that's right. I think part of it's the rate story, and then of course, part of it is how long can we compound at this 20% plus earnings growth story, right? It's been a great stretch. If you get the productivity from AI in the coming years, you see corporate margins stay healthy, I think that story stays intact. You climb that wall of worry on 2027 and 2028, and that's probably the path higher for the tech sector. Chris Hussey: All right, great. Let's put a bow on it. What's the trade? Peter Callahan: Yeah, I got two things in focus, right? One, of course, semiconductors. We talked about it, but that's a group that hasn't gone anywhere for a while. Multiples have compressed, and we kind of talked about this sort of personal assistant, consumer AI story starting to pick up over the last couple of weeks. So I'll be watching for semiconductors into 3Q earnings to hopefully find its footing again. And then the other one, consumer services and consumer experiences. Consumer stocks had one of their biggest months of underperformance in over 10 years in the month of September. Of course, rates and oil weigh heavy on the group, but you could argue that's an opportunity to climb a wall of worry down the stretch of 2026. And that'll be an area I would start to reengage and sharpen pencils, and find some good idiosyncratic ideas. Chris Hussey: In the tech world, does that mean e-commerce? What do they mean? Peter Callahan: Yeah, exactly. Internet services, commerce, and then some of the live events and experiences that we have in the sector. Chris Hussey: All right. What are you watching for in the month ahead? Peter Callahan: Yeah, of course. So early month macro data, right? We have a Fed meet at the end of this month. Right now the market has about a 40% chance of a hike priced in. So we'll see if the macro data tilts that one way or the other. We'll kick off corporate earnings in the middle of the month. Of course, all about finding that return on invested capital vis-a-vis AI, both in the tech sector, but of course outside of the tech sector as well, increasingly important. And then finally, we have midterm elections some 30-odd days away. That'll sort of be in the background as we head into earnings season, and so that'll be something to watch as well. Chris Hussey: Pete, thanks so much for joining us. Really appreciate it. Chris Hussey: That does it for this week's episode of The Markets. I'm Chris Hussey. Thanks for listening.
